It doesn't specify: (a) which field in the error body to match (`error.type`, `error.message`, the raw body string), (b) what keyword to search for (`'temperature is deprecated'`? `'temperature'`? `'sampling'`?), or (c) where in the call stack this translation fires (inside `failure.py`'s `_map_http` which already handles 400s, in `bedrock_model.py`'s builder, or as a wrapper in `runner.py`'s broad-except path).
findings.location: Approach / Decision C — 'translate it into an actionable error'; Scope / `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py`
scenarios: Implementer keys on 'ValidationException' alone — catches unrelated Bedrock 400s (e.g., malformed JSON) and mistranslates them as temperature errors.

Implementer places translation in failure.py — the module already handles 400 → CHANGE_SETTINGS but the new actionable message is then separate from the resolution class, creating two divergent signals.

findings.finding: The `supports_temperature` capability override cannot target specific Bedrock model IDs using the current profile-predicate table: `BedrockModelProfile` does not carry a per-model identifier field that predicates can read, so a predicate cannot distinguish `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (temperature fatal) from `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (temperature fine). Setting `supports_temperature=False` for all Bedrock Claude models (the only expressible predicate) would strip temperature from sonnet-4-6 too, breaking the greedy Pass-2 determinism the plan specifically calls out as a motivation for keeping temperature on working models.
findings.location: Approach / Decision C — 'Add `supports_temperature: bool` to `ModelCapabilities` … add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock models'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `_BEDROCK_TEMPERATURE_UNSUPPORTED: frozenset[str]` set in `capabilities.py` (or `bedrock_model.py`) listing confirmed-fatal model IDs (initially `{'us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7', 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7'}`). In `capabilities_for`, when the model is a string, check it against this set and set `supports_temperature=False` directly — bypassing the profile-predicate path for this one capability. This keeps the decision in the capability module (not runner.py), handles model-ID-level precision, and is extensible as more models are measured.

findings.finding: Decision C specifies adding a `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicate to withdraw `supports_temperature` for 'the affected Bedrock models' (specifically `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`), but the plan never defines what predicate expression can discriminate a specific Bedrock model ID within a family without importing botocore. The existing `_is_claude` predicate uses `bedrock_thinking_variant` (a family-level field), and `BedrockModelProfile` carries no per-model-ID attribute accessible in the boto3-free path. The decision rule references 'a rebar override entry' but the predicate vocabulary for that entry is unspecified.
findings.location: Approach — Decision C; src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py `_REBAR_OVERRIDES`

findings.finding: Decision C adds `supports_temperature: bool` to `ModelCapabilities` with an override for 'the affected Bedrock models' (specifically `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`), using the existing predicate/override table in `_REBAR_OVERRIDES`. However, the override table predicates receive a `ModelProfile` object — and `BedrockModelProfile` does not carry a per-model-id string. The plan does not specify what profile attribute or mechanism the predicate will inspect to distinguish `claude-opus-4-7` (temperature-fatal) from `claude-sonnet-4-6` (temperature-ok). The existing predicate `_is_claude` tests the profile's TYPE and `bedrock_thinking_variant` field, neither of which is model-specific.
findings.location: Scope / Decision C — 'add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock models'; capabilities.py override table

findings.finding: Decision B introduces a new warning 'when caching was requested but both cache counters are zero,' but the plan does not specify (a) where the check is placed — a new branch in `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`, a new function, or inline at the call site in `runner.py`; (b) the exact triggering condition — whether it requires `caps.prompt_cache_style == 'bedrock'` (or `!= 'none'`) as a guard, or fires purely on counter values; (c) whether `caps` must be threaded into `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` (which currently only takes `usage: dict`). Without this, two implementers will produce different call signatures and different false-positive profiles.
findings.location: Approach — Decision B; AC 'a test asserts rebar WARNS when caching was requested but both cache counters are zero'; src/rebar/llm/runner.py `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`
